Beyond Basic Biology
Our department redefines multidisciplinary when it comes to our educational and research opportunities. Evolutionary Biology, Genetics, Microbiology, Paleontology, and Toxicology encompass only a few of the exciting areas in which our faculty and students are impacting global scientific challenges.
Dr. Christa Baker Awarded $1.5 million NSF Grant
Dr. Christa Baker, Assistant Professor of Biological Sciences, was recently awarded a 5-year, $1.5 million grant from the National Science Foundation (NSF) to investigate how brains recognize sounds. This award will advance STEM workforce training and educator development by training 5 undergraduate students, a PhD student, a postdoctoral researcher, and 6 high school teachers in the latest neuroscience research techniques.
Read more
Dr. Lindsay Zanno Receives the 2026 North Carolina Award
On November 17, 2026 at the Lenovo Center Governor Josh Stein will present the state’s highest civilian honor, 2026 North Carolina Award, to Dr. Lindsay Zanno for her world-renowned paleontology research program and public outreach.

RECENT BIOLOGICAL Sciences award winners
Dr. Michaela Gazdik Stofer Wins 2026 Outstanding Research Mentor Award
The Outstanding Research Mentor Award is given to one NCSU faculty mentor per year across the entire university. This award is driven by undergraduate student nominations and highlights mentors that serve as a guide, create opportunities, encourage communication, support student belonging, and offer academic/career advice.
Read more
Emily Phillips Wins 2026 Yusor Abu-Salha Senior Award for Outstanding Community Engagement
Biological Sciences graduating senior won the Yusor Abu-Salha Senior Award for Outstanding Community Engagement at the 2026 COS Senior Recognition Event.
Read more
Dr. Stefanie Chen Wins 2026 University Outstanding Teaching Award
Biological Sciences teaching faculty Dr. Stefanie Chen received the 2026 University Outstanding Teaching Award, which recognizes teaching excellence from across the university.

Enriching the Student Experience Beyond the Classroom and Campus
Because so much critical learning occurs outside of the classroom, we have partnerships with communities and institutions across the state and are expanding our study abroad offerings to provide exciting opportunities for exploration, research, and engagement. The Biological Sciences study abroad program included 116 NC State students and partnerships with seven countries in Summer 2025 and 2026.
Read more about Study Abroad
Plagues, History, and Public Health in Prague
This summer study abroad program is based on MB 200: The Fourth Horseman: Plagues that Changed the World. Students will learn about the role of plague doctors, tour the Jewish quarter, examine life under medieval quarantine, and analyze plague art and architecture. Visits include Prague Castle, plague columns in the city, the National Museum, and the Terezin Memorial. Applications for Summer 2027 open on October 1, 2026.
Read more about this opportunity
NEWS from 2026
Celebrating Dana Derosier’s 24 Years at NC State
Dana Derosier is retiring on January 1, 2027, following more than 24 years of dedicated service to NC State University. Serving as University Program Specialist and Executive Assistant to the Department Head in Biological Sciences, Dana has been a vital anchor for our community.
Read more
2026 Biological Sciences Promotions
Promotion and tenure mark major milestones in the academic lives of NC State faculty. Promoted faculty have met rigorous standards in their realms of responsibility, and tenured faculty have made a significant impact in their discipline.
Read more
Dr. William “Bill” Grant’s Family Speaks at Spring 2026 Graduation
On May 8, 2026 the Department of Biological Sciences celebrated the graduation of 480 undergraduate majors, 274 undergraduate minors, and 9 graduate students. Closing remarks were delivered by Dr. John Meitzen and Paul Grant, who presented a donation to the William C. Grant Scholarship in honor of his late father.
Read more
2026 National Association for Interpretation Conference Recipient
Congratulations to Jonah Peckham, one of our Master’s students in Integrative Biology, on receiving a full scholarship to attend this year’s National Association for Interpretation conference. Jonah will present his research on zoo programming designed to foster empathy and strengthen conservation values among visitors.
The Humanities Hire That Helps STEM Students
Freha Legoas, graduate services coordinator for the Department of Biological Sciences, found her career helping STEM students and problem-solving in academic administration.
Read more
Biological Sciences Teaching Professor Dr. Marian Gardner to Retire
Dr. Marian B. Gardner (“Betty”) is retiring on July 1, 2026 after 37 years of exemplary teaching, scholarly activity, and service at NC State University. She has earned the title of Emeritus Professor of Teaching at NC State University. We are highly appreciative of her contributions and wish her well in the next stage of her life.
Read more
BioSci and NC State – a national hub for Environmental Health Sciences research
We are one of very few institutions to support several major Centers funded by the National Institutes of Environmental Health Sciences of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to improve understanding about chemical exposures in the environment, their health impacts, and prevention.
